_requireApprovingReview: TRUE since 2026-10-06, the day the reviewer first worked here (powerreviewer reviewed #469). Before that it was false by an explicit decision of 2026-08-22, which merged on green CI alone — a weaker bar, since nothing read the diff but the test suite. A review reaches this repo ONLY by homelab's poll backstop (personal/agent-review.yml), not by a request-review job in ci.yml: this repo is PUBLIC and homelab is PRIVATE, and a public repo cannot call a private repo's reusable workflow — GitHub resolves the callee when it creates the run, before any job-level `if`, so such a job fails the whole workflow to load (tried 2026-08-22; run 32594475090 completed with zero jobs). Two consequences: a review arrives within a poll interval (~15 min) rather than immediately, and the poll only picks up PRs carrying the reviewLabel. pr:land adds that label when it opens the PR; a PR opened with bare `gh pr create` and no label is never reviewed and would wait here until reviewTimeoutMs (#436–#468 went unreviewed that way).
_maxReviewRounds: A round is a REQUEST_CHANGES review — approvals spend none. Three, mirroring ordago: every round is a paid agentic run on the homelab reviewer, and past three the marginal round stopped paying there.
_roundsExhausted: "merge" — the cap ENDS the review conversation and the PR lands on CI green alone; nothing is left to ask the user, so an agent must not stop to report that the rounds ran out. Narrow on purpose: red CI still exits 10, and a Breaking-Client: trailer still exits 30 however many rounds were spent. "handoff" (the shared default) makes the cap open a human conversation instead.
_reviewTimeoutMs: 40 min per head: one ~15-min poll interval, plus the reviewer's own agentic run, plus a missed poll's slack. Shorter would exit 30 on a review that was merely on its way; the timeout is reset by every new head, so a fix push after REQUEST_CHANGES gets the full window again.
_ciPaths: ci.yml has NO paths: filter — it runs on every push and PR to develop/beta/main. '**' says that directly; enumerating top-level directories would silently stop being true the moment one is added.
_sharedBlastRadius: DORMANT while develop requires a merge queue (docs/decisions/merge-queue.md): pr:land detects the queue and never rebases for staleness. These paths apply only if the queue is switched off, when a base move here forces a rebase even with no direct file overlap.
_hardStop: File paths that never self-merge. EMPTY by the user's decision of 2026-10-05 (AGENTS.md, Approval and Autonomy contract): consent covers what is subjective, so rules, indexes, converters and backfill scripts merge on CI green + ai-review like any other code — none of them reaches beta or prod from develop; they get there only through a promotion PR the user merges. What still exits 30 is the Breaking-Client: trailer (hardStopTrailerSource's default) and any PR not based on develop. Add a pattern only for a path whose merge alone, with no promotion in between, changes something users or production data see.
